question: The header's Sources field names hsdd/context/prd-simple-login.md (US-1, US-2, US-3, Screens) and hsdd/context/update-1-add-phone.md (AC-2.1 amended, AC-2.4, Screen, Scope), both superseded by PRD v2 (Q-038, Q-049). How does the citation touch move them, and does the moved entry also gain the PRD v2 sections the node's own text now cites?

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, each section to its counterpart
options.consequence: The header reads byte for byte as the root's embedded copy S12 wrote (DEC-107), so nothing differs before H17's version ripple. The field still lacks US-4 to US-6, which the Overview cites, until H16 adds them.

options.label: one PRD v2 entry, plus the newly cited sections
options.consequence: The field is complete now, but the touch adds citations rather than moving them, and the header then differs from the embedded copy, which this step cannot write, until H17.

chosen: one PRD v2 entry, each section to its counterpart
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch moves a node's Sources entry for a source document to the current version and changes only citations. PRD v2's header supersedes prd-simple-login.md together with update-1-add-phone.md, so one entry replaces both. PRD 1's US-1, US-2, US-3 and Screens have PRD v2 sections of the same names; Update 1's AC-2.1 amended and AC-2.4 sit inside PRD v2 US-2, its Screen is PRD v2 Screens and its Scope is PRD v2 Scope. The union is (US-1, US-2, US-3, Screens, Scope), the mapping S12 used for the embedded copy (Q-049) and S13 used for the backend (DEC-117). PRD v2 Screens draws Home and Rooms only, so the Login screen is governed by PRD v2 US-1 alone; PRD 1's Login wireframe stays the history of shipped simple-login.web.2. The intake record's Sources and Scope paragraph gives newly governing sections to each phase-plan-append, so they go to H16 as a consider. Had the intake record left the additions to the citation touch, the second option would have led.

question: The Phase Plan's Decisions D1 to D5 sit outside every phase section. D3 cites '(AC-1.2)' and '(AC-2.3)' with no document, written on 2026-10-30 when PRD 1 was the only PRD; D1 cites profile-api@v1. Q-038 (S10) calls D1 to D5 history. Are they history, and if live, do D3's bare ids move?

options.label: live; qualify D3's two ids as PRD v2
options.consequence: D3 reads '(PRD v2 AC-1.2)' and '(PRD v2 AC-2.3)'; a later phase that cites D3 carries an explicit current source into its context. The sentence stays true: PRD v2 AC-1.2 and AC-2.3 are word for word PRD 1's. D1's profile-api@v1 stays (a live earlier version).

options.label: live; leave D3's ids bare
options.consequence: No edit; the bare ids resolve through the moved Sources field to PRD v2. A reader of a phase context, which carries cited D{n} but not the node's Sources, sees ids with no document.

options.label: history in full, as Q-038 reads it
options.consequence: Nothing in D1 to D5 moves; but H16 revisits D4 (DEC-012) and Q-037 asks it to revisit D1, so they plainly still govern the node.

chosen: live; qualify D3's two ids as PRD v2
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch moves a live citation of a superseded version, including any sentence that states what holds now, and treats only shipped phases and dated or historical text as history. D1 to D5 are node decisions in force: hsdd-phase-plan's phase context carries the D{n} a phase's lines cite, and the intake record has H16 revisit D4 (DEC-012). D3's bare ids were written against PRD 1, as S13 counted the bare '(AC-2.4)' in a shipped backend phase as an Update 1 citation. S12 qualified the root's bare '(AC-1.2)' the same way (DEC-109). The later 'the AC-1.2 message' in D3 refers back to the message D3 just cited and is left. '(Added at the simple-login.web.2 gate, 2026-10-30.)' is a dated provenance marker and stays. Had phase contexts carried the node's Sources, leaving the ids bare would have led.

question: The file cites profile-api@v1 seven times: the header's Consumes line, the Overview ('The node knows the backend only through auth-api@v1 and profile-api@v1, which simple-login.web.4 replaces with profile-api@v2, and booking-api@v1'), D1 ('profile-api@v1 makes an expired token indistinguishable from an unknown one'), simple-login.web.1's and simple-login.web.3's Consumes, simple-login.web.4's Scope, and the phase graph's fixture box feeding simple-login.web.1. profile-api@v1 is stable, not deprecated, coexisting with v2. What does the touch do with them, and where does the one consider item go?

options.label: leave all seven; one consider to simple-login.web
options.consequence: The web's next planning (H16) and its reconcile (H17) see one item naming profile-api@v2: D1 can cite profile-api@v2 G7 when Q-037's revisit of D1 lands, and the ripple keeps v1 in Consumes while web.1 and web.3 name it.

options.label: leave all seven; consider to simple-login.backend
options.consequence: Joins Q-056 at the producer, but the citing sentences here are about this consumer's own boundary and decision, which only the web's planning can restate.

options.label: restate the Overview and D1 to name profile-api@v2
options.consequence: Moves citations of a live earlier version, which the citation-touch rule forbids; the Overview would also drop the true account that web.4 replaced v1.

chosen: leave all seven; one consider to simple-login.web
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch: an earlier version that is neither deprecated nor retired stays live beside the new one, so every citation of it is left, and one consider item naming the new version goes to the node whose plan would move to it, the node of the citing phase or the consumer the citing sentence is about. Every citing phase and sentence here is about simple-login.web. The Consumes line is reconcile's in any case, and web.1, web.3 and web.4 are shipped (verification docs on main), so four of the seven are history. Both live sentences stay true: profile-api@v2's Versioning says GET /api/me serves v2 only from the producer's v2 phase, and its consumers are web.4 and integration.2, so 'replaces' holds; profile-api@v1's G-rule on rejection and profile-api@v2 G7 both say an expired token cannot be told from an unknown one. S13 sent the producer's item to simple-login.backend (DEC-118, Q-056). A web phase still planned on v1 would have made that phase's handoff the target instead.

question: The Overview's first sentence reads 'with three screens (PRD v2 Screens)', and PRD v2 Screens draws Home and Rooms only; Login is PRD v2 US-1's, which the next sentence cites (Q-049). The citation already names the current version. Does this citation touch tighten it to '(PRD v2 US-1, Screens)'?

options.label: leave it
options.consequence: The touch stays inside the rule; the paragraph remains true read as a whole, since the next sentence cites PRD v2 US-1 for Login and PRD v2 names the Login screen in AC-1.2.

options.label: add US-1 to the parenthetical
options.consequence: The sentence verifies alone against PRD v2, at the cost of a citation touch editing a citation that names no superseded version, outside what the rule moves.

why: The dispatch asks for hsdd-spec's citation-touch rule exactly, and that rule moves citations of superseded versions; this one, written by S10 under DEC-089, already names PRD v2. Read with the sentences beside it, the paragraph says nothing PRD v2 contradicts: PRD v2 has three screens (Login in AC-1.2, Home in US-2, Rooms in AC-4.1), Screens draws two, and Login's sentence cites US-1. The same holds for 'offers Book a room, which opens Rooms', cited to US-2, US-3 and US-6, whose button PRD v2 Screens draws. Had the Overview cited no source for Login at all, adding US-1 would have led.

question: Q-034 to Q-037 target H16, simple-login.web's phase-plan-append, and reached this citation touch only because H16's target is the same node (B-10); the step must close every routed item, and a closed item no longer reaches H16. How are they closed?

options.label: close each as explained and carry its text to H16
options.consequence: H16 receives every item whole with the same kind; the queue gains four new ids, the churn DEC-087 already logged as an hsdd-auto defect.

options.label: close each as addressed
options.consequence: Claims work this step did not do: a citation touch changes only citations, and every item is Phase Plan content; H16 would never see them.

chosen: close each as explained and carry its text to H16
why: hsdd-spec's citation touch changes only citations and the sentences they sit in, so none of these plan items (the time module and its tests, the fetch stub against booking-api@v1's fixtures, timeZone in the web's Profile type and its absence, D4's revisit and D1 against booking-api@v1 G16) can be addressed here, and the dispatch requires every routed item closed. S09, S10, S11 and S13 met the same mechanics and the orchestrator kept the carry (DEC-085, DEC-095, DEC-103, DEC-119, DEC-121). Each carried text keeps the item's original text verbatim, so its trail back to S04, S05, S07 and S10 survives. A way for an item on H16 to wait for H16 would have changed this.

question: How does this citation touch classify against the touched artifact's own versioning rules?

options.label: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
options.consequence: The node keeps its id, Kind, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, phases and every phase section; no contract or ADR file changes, so neither INDEX is regenerated.

options.label: a change for hsdd-reconcile to drain
options.consequence: Would add a Governance updates entry for a Sources move and two qualified ids that no contract or consumer can observe.

chosen: compatible wording change, nothing versioned moves
why: hsdd-spec asks for the classification as one decision. Two edits: the header's Sources line, two baseline entries becoming one PRD v2 entry with the same sections' counterparts (DEC-122), and D3's '(AC-1.2)' and '(AC-2.3)' qualified as PRD v2, whose text is word for word the same (DEC-123). No sentence was restated, no decision's rule changed, and Kind, Purpose, Owns, Does not own, Consumes, Produces, Governed by, Decomposes into, Isolation strategy, Overview, the phase table and every phase section are byte for byte as before. A node spec has no version of its own. Had a Consumes line needed to change, it would have gone to hsdd-reconcile instead.

question: The web's Overview says 'three screens (PRD v2 Screens)', but PRD v2 Screens draws only Home and Rooms; Login is governed by US-1 (S14's DEC-125 left it, medium). Rework S14, route it, or leave it?

options.label: Route a consider item to simple-login.web
options.consequence: The consistency stage's spec-touch on the web, which other open items on the node already call for, changes the citation to (PRD v2 US-1, Screens); S14 stands.

options.label: Rework S14
options.consequence: A citation touch would restate a sentence another step wrote, which its rule forbids.

options.label: Leave it
options.consequence: A citation that does not support its sentence stays in a live header.

chosen: Route a consider item to simple-login.web
why: The sentence was written by S10 and is wrong only in its citation, not in substance; a citation touch may not restate it, and the web node already has open items that bring a consistency spec-touch. A sentence false in substance would have changed this to a must-address.

question: S14's report lists reads outside its inputs (verification docs, the web's code, earlier step records). Keep the output or rework?

options.label: Rework without those reads
options.consequence: The step could not tell shipped phases from live text, which decides what moves.

why: Telling shipped phases from live text needs the verification docs; all reads are inside the repository and none is out of bounds. A read outside the repository would have changed this.
